modelAudit.summary: The generated FULL_CHAPTER lesson for Class 8 Science 'Chemical Effects of Electric Current' is fully compliant with NCERT canonical content, catalog rules, and pedagogical guidelines. All core concepts—including conductivity of liquids, weak current detection via LEDs and magnetic testers, chemical effects (electrolysis & potato terminal detector), and electroplating mechanism and applications—are thoroughly and accurately covered with faithful activity procedures, correct scientific claims, and accurate page citations.

majorConcepts.concept: Electrical Conductivity of Liquids (Good vs Poor Conductors)
majorConcepts.explanation: Accurately defines good/poor conductors in liquid form and explains why the classification as 'good/poor' is preferred over binary 'conductor/insulator'.

majorConcepts.concept: Detection of Weak Currents (LED and Magnetic Testers)
majorConcepts.explanation: Explains why weak currents fail to light standard bulb filaments and details both LED polarity rules and magnetic needle compass tester construction.

majorConcepts.concept: Conduction in Aqueous Solutions (Distilled vs Tap water, Acids, Bases, Salts)
majorConcepts.explanation: Explains how presence of dissolved salts, acids, or bases renders distilled water conductive, citing relevant textbook safety precautions.

majorConcepts.concept: Chemical Effects of Electric Current (Electrolysis, Gas Bubbles, Potato Spot)
majorConcepts.explanation: Covers William Nicholson's 1800 electrolysis discovery (O2 at positive, H2 at negative electrode) and Boojho's potato positive-terminal detector.
Thoroughly explains CuSO4 dissociation, deposition of copper on the negative electrode (cathode), and replenishment from the positive copper plate (anode).

majorConcepts.concept: Applications and Environmental Concerns of Electroplating
majorConcepts.explanation: Covers commercial uses (chromium, zinc, tin, gold/silver) and details the polluting nature of conducting solution waste.
